article.title: China, BRICS & Brazil: what Lula vs. Bolsonaro means for the Global South
article.author: Amanda Yee
article.content: As Brazil heads into the October 25 runoff election between President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Flávio Bolsonaro, the country stands as a crucial battleground in Washington’s strategy to contain China, as well as global geopolitics. What does this election mean for the future of China-Brazil ties, the BRICS alliance, and independent technological sovereignty across the Global South? Tings Chak – researcher, writer, and art director for the Tricontinental: Institute for Social Research – joins Amanda Yee to break down the two competing paths for Brazil represented by Lula and Bolsonaro. Read Chak’s article: “How Brazil’s election could reshape relations with China”
